facts.fact: The Government of Burundi's own report states that ordinary registration continues as usual although the civil-status services 'currently' suffer from a lack of computerised data; the report gives no date for the statement, so its date of receipt by the UN, 3 December 2021, is used rather than its 2025 publication date.

systems.platform: none stated; the report says the services lack computerised data
systems.tiers: the civil-status office of the mother's domicile, where a birth is declared within fifteen days; provincial civil-status controllers

note: The value 'paper' is the nearest closed value to the report's words (a lack of computerised data); the report does not use the word paper. Also stated, with no aspect to carry it: a national ad hoc steering committee chaired by the First Vice-President, functional since 2014; distance from civil-status offices listed first among causes of non-registration; 84% of under-fives registered (EDS 2016-2017), from 54% in Kirundo to 94% in Gitega.
